sanskrit: yad idaṃ vaiśvadevānte sāyaṃprātaḥ pradīyate tad dattvātithibhṛtyebhyo rājañ śeṣeṇa jīvasi
english: That which is offered at the close of the Vaiśvadeva rite morning and evening — having given that to guests and servants, O king, you live on what remains.

sanskrit: iṣṭayaḥ paśubandhāś ca kāmyanaimittikāś ca ye vartante pākayajñāś ca yajñakarma ca nityadā
english: Sacrificial rites, animal offerings, optional and occasional ceremonies, domestic fire sacrifices, and the daily performance of sacrificial duties — all these continue.

sanskrit: asminn api mahāraṇye vijane dasyusevite rāṣṭrād apetya vasato dhārmas te nāvasīdati
english: Even here in this great wilderness, desolate and frequented by bandits, though you have left your kingdom and dwell in exile, your dharma does not decay.

sanskrit: aśvamedho rājasūyaḥ puṇḍarīko 'tha gosavaḥ etair api mahāyajñair iṣṭaṃ te bhūridakṣiṇaiḥ
english: The Aśvamedha, the Rājasūya, the Puṇḍarīka, and the Gosava — you have performed even these great sacrifices with abundant gifts of honor.

sanskrit: rājan parītayā buddhyā viṣame 'kṣaparājaye rājyaṃ vasūny āyudhāni bhrātṝn māṃ cāsi nirjitaḥ
english: O king, with a clouded mind at the calamitous dice defeat, you were vanquished — your kingdom, your wealth, your weapons, your brothers, and even me.

sanskrit: ṛjor mṛdor vadānyasya hrīmataḥ satyavādinaḥ katham akṣavyasanajā buddhir āpatitā tava
english: For one who is upright, gentle, generous, modest, and truthful — how did a mind born of addiction to dice come to descend upon you?

sanskrit: atīva moham āyāti manaś ca paridūyate niśāmya te duḥkham idam imāṃ cāpadam īdṛśīm
english: Extreme delusion overtakes me and my heart is seared within, witnessing this suffering of yours and such a calamity as this.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam īśvarasya vaśe lokas tiṣṭhate nātmano yathā
english: On this topic they cite this ancient tale: the world abides under the sway of the Lord, not under the power of one's own self.

sanskrit: dhātaiva khalu bhūtānāṃ sukhaduḥkhe priyāpriye dadhāti sarvam īśānaḥ purastāc chukram uccaran
english: The Creator alone indeed apportions pleasure and pain, the pleasant and the unpleasant, for all beings — the Lord who is supreme, who emits the seed from the beginning.

sanskrit: yathā dārumayī yoṣā naravīra samāhitā īrayaty aṅgam aṅgāni tathā rājann imāḥ prajāḥ
english: Just as a wooden puppet, O hero among men, when set in motion, moves its limb after limb, so too, O king, does He move these creatures.

sanskrit: ākāśa iva bhūtāni vyāpya sarvāṇi bhārata īśvaro vidadhātīha kalyāṇaṃ yac ca pāpakam
english: Like the sky pervading all beings, O descendant of Bharata, the Lord here ordains both the auspicious and the evil.

sanskrit: śakunis tantubaddho vā niyato 'yam anīśvaraḥ īśvarasya vaśe tiṣṭhan nānyeṣāṃ nātmanaḥ prabhuḥ
english: Like a bird bound by a string, this creature is controlled and powerless; standing under the sway of the Lord, it is master neither of others nor of itself.

sanskrit: maṇiḥ sūtra iva proto nasyota iva govṛṣaḥ dhātur ādeśam anveti tanmayo hi tadarpaṇaḥ
english: Like a gem threaded on a string, like a bull led by the nose-rope — it follows the Creator's command, for it is constituted of Him alone and wholly surrendered to Him.

sanskrit: nātmādhīno manuṣyo 'yaṃ kālaṃ bhavati kaṃ cana srotaso madhyam āpannaḥ kūlād vṛkśa iva cyutaḥ
english: This human being is not self-governed for any span of time, like a tree fallen from its bank into the midst of a current.

sanskrit: ajño jantur anīśo 'yam ātmanaḥ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ īśvaraprerito gacchet svargaṃ narakam eva ca
english: This ignorant creature is not master of its own pleasure and pain; impelled by the Lord, it may go to heaven or even to hell.

sanskrit: yathā vāyos tṛṇāgrāṇi vaśaṃ yānti balīyasaḥ dhātur evaṃ vaśaṃ yānti sarvabhūtāni bhārata
english: Just as the tips of grass come under the sway of the mighty wind, so all beings come under the sway of the Creator, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: āryakarmaṇi yuñjānaḥ pāpe vā punar īśvaraḥ vyāpya bhūtāni carate na cāyam iti lakṣyate
english: Engaging beings in noble actions or again in sin, the Lord pervades and moves through all creatures — yet He is not perceived as such.

sanskrit: hetumātram idaṃ dhātuḥ śarīraṃ kṣetrasaṃjñitam yena kārayate karma śubhāśubhaphalaṃ vibhuḥ
english: This body, known as the field, is merely the instrument of the Creator — through it the all-pervading Lord causes actions of auspicious and inauspicious fruit to be performed.

sanskrit: paśya māyāprabhāvo 'yam īśvareṇa yathā kṛtaḥ yo hanti bhūtair bhūtāni mohayitvātmamāyayā
english: Behold this power of illusion fashioned by the Lord — He who slays beings by means of other beings, having deluded them with His own māyā.

sanskrit: anyathā paridṛṣṭāni munibhir vedadarśibhiḥ anyathā parivartante vegā iva nabhasvataḥ
english: Things are seen one way by the sages who behold the Veda, yet they turn out otherwise — like the gusts of the wind.

sanskrit: anyathaiva hi manyante puruṣās tāni tāni ca anyathaiva prabhus tāni karoti vikaroti ca
english: Men indeed think of those various things one way, yet the Lord makes and unmakes them in quite another way.

sanskrit: yathā kāṣṭhena vā kāṣṭham aśmānaṃ cāśmanā punaḥ ayasā cāpy ayaś chindyān nirviceṣṭam acetanam
english: Just as wood may be split by wood, stone by stone, and iron by iron — all inert and insensate —

sanskrit: evaṃ sa bhagavān devaḥ svayambhūḥ prapitāmahaḥ hinasti bhūtair bhūtāni chadma kṛtvā yudhiṣṭhira
english: — so that blessed God, the Self-Existent, the great Progenitor, slays beings by means of other beings, assuming a disguise, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: saṃprayojya viyojyāyaṃ kāmakārakaraḥ prabhuḥ krīḍate bhagavan bhūtair bālaḥ krīḍanakair iva
english: Joining and separating — this Lord who acts as He wills, the Blessed One, sports with beings as a child with toys.

sanskrit: na mātṛpitṛvad rājan dhātā bhūteṣu vartate roṣād iva pravṛtto 'yaṃ yathāyam itaro janaḥ
english: The Creator does not behave toward creatures as a mother or father would, O king; He acts as if impelled by wrath, like any ordinary person.

sanskrit: āryāñ śīlavato dṛṣṭvā hrīmato vṛttikarśitān anāryān sukhinaś caiva vihvalāmīva cintayā
english: Seeing the noble, the virtuous, the modest ground down in livelihood, while the ignoble are prosperous — I am overwhelmed, as it were, with anguish.

sanskrit: tavemām āpadaṃ dṛṣṭvā samṛddhiṃ ca suyodhane dhātāraṃ garhaye pārtha viṣamaṃ yo 'nupaśyati
english: Seeing this calamity of yours and the prosperity of Suyodhana, I reproach the Creator, O Pārtha, who looks on unequally.

sanskrit: āryaśāstrātige krūre lubdhe dharmāpacāyini dhārtarāṣṭre śriyaṃ dattvā dhātā kiṃ phalam aśnute
english: Having bestowed fortune on the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, who transgresses the codes of the noble, who is cruel, greedy, and contemptuous of dharma — what fruit does the Creator enjoy?

sanskrit: karma cet kṛtam anveti kartāraṃ nānyam ṛcchati karmaṇā tena pāpena lipyate nūnam īśvaraḥ
english: If the deed follows its doer and does not go to another, then surely the Lord is stained by that sinful act.

sanskrit: atha karma kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ na cet kartāram ṛcchati kāraṇaṃ balam eveha janāñ śocāmi durbalān
english: Or if a sinful deed done does not return to its doer, then mere force is the only cause in this world — and I grieve for the powerless.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca valgu citrapadaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ yājñaseni tvayā vacaḥ uktaṃ tac chrutam asmābhir nāstikyaṃ tu prabhāṣase
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O Yājñasenī, what you have spoken is eloquent, adorned with varied phrases, and smooth — we have heard it; yet you speak in the manner of an atheist.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ dharmaphalānveṣī rājaputri carāmy uta dadāmi deyam ity eva yaje yaṣṭavyam ity uta
english: I do not practice dharma in quest of its fruits, O princess; I give because it is to be given, I sacrifice because it is to be sacrificed.

sanskrit: astu vātra phalaṃ mā vā kartavyaṃ puruṣeṇa yat gṛhān āvasatā kṛṣṇe yathāśakti karomi tat
english: Whether there be fruit in this or not — whatever a man living as a householder ought to do, O Kṛṣṇā, I do that to the best of my ability.

sanskrit: dharmaṃ carāmi suśroṇi na dharmaphalakāraṇāt āgamān anatikramya satāṃ vṛttam avekṣya ca dharma eva manaḥ kṛṣṇe svabhāvāc caiva me dhṛtam
english: I practice dharma, O fair-hipped one, not for the sake of its fruit; not transgressing the scriptures, looking to the conduct of the virtuous — it is dharma alone, O Kṛṣṇā, to which my mind is held by its very nature.

sanskrit: na dharmaphalam āpnoti yo dharmaṃ dogdhum icchati yaś cainaṃ śaṅkate kṛtvā nāstikyāt pāpacetanaḥ
english: He who wishes to milk dharma of its fruit does not attain the fruit of dharma; and he who, after practicing it, doubts it out of atheism, being of sinful mind — he too does not.

sanskrit: ativādān madāc caiva mā dharmam atiśaṅkithāḥ dharmātiśaṅkī puruṣas tiryaggatiparāyaṇaḥ
english: Do not excessively doubt dharma out of arrogance or pride; a man who excessively doubts dharma is destined for the state of beasts.

sanskrit: dharmo yasyātiśaṅkyaḥ syād ārṣaṃ vā durbalātmanaḥ vedāc chūdra ivāpeyāt sa lokād ajarāmarāt
english: He of weak spirit for whom dharma or the teaching of the seers would be a matter of excessive doubt — he falls away from the undying, undecaying world, as a śūdra falls away from the Veda.

sanskrit: vedādhyāyī dharmaparaḥ kule jāto yaśasvini sthavireṣu sa yoktavyo rājabhir dharmacāribhiḥ
english: One who is a student of the Veda, devoted to dharma, born of an illustrious family — him should kings who walk in dharma employ among the elders.

sanskrit: pāpīyān hi sa śūdrebhyas taskarebhyo viśeṣataḥ śāstrātigo mandabuddhir yo dharmam atiśaṅkate
english: He is more wicked than śūdras — especially more so than thieves — that dull-witted transgressor of scripture who excessively doubts dharma.

sanskrit: pratyakṣaṃ hi tvayā dṛṣṭa ṛṣir gacchan mahātapāḥ mārkaṇḍeyo 'prameyātmā dharmeṇa cirajīvitām
english: For you have seen with your own eyes the great ascetic, the seer Mārkaṇḍeya of immeasurable spirit, who has attained long life through dharma.

sanskrit: vyāso vasiṣṭho maitreyo nārado lomaśaḥ śukaḥ anye ca ṛṣayaḥ siddhā dharmeṇaiva sucetasaḥ
english: Vyāsa, Vasiṣṭha, Maitreya, Nārada, Lomaśa, Śuka, and other accomplished seers of pure minds — all have attained perfection through dharma alone.

sanskrit: pratyakṣaṃ paśyasi hy etān divyayogasamanvitān śāpānugrahaṇe śaktān devair api garīyasaḥ
english: You see these very ones with your own eyes — endowed with divine yoga, capable of curse and benediction, weightier even than the gods.

sanskrit: ete hi dharmam evādau varṇayanti sadā mama kartavyam amaraprakhyāḥ pratyakṣāgamabuddhayaḥ
english: These very ones, resplendent as immortals, whose understanding is grounded in direct scriptural knowledge, always declare dharma first as what must be done by me.

sanskrit: ato nārhasi kalyāṇi dhātāraṃ dharmam eva ca rajomūḍhena manasā kṣeptuṃ śaṅkitum eva ca
english: Therefore, O auspicious one, you should not revile the Creator or dharma itself with a mind clouded by passion, nor should you doubt them.

sanskrit: dharmātiśaṅkī nānyasmin pramāṇam adhigacchati ātmapramāṇa unnaddhaḥ śreyaso hy avamanyakaḥ
english: He who excessively doubts dharma finds no authority in anything else; puffed up with himself as his own authority, he is contemptuous of the good.

sanskrit: indriyaprītisaṃbaddhaṃ yad idaṃ lokasākṣikam etāvān manyate bālo moham anyatra gacchati
english: The fool thinks that only this — what is witnessed by the world and bound up with the pleasure of the senses — is all there is, and falls into delusion regarding what lies beyond.

sanskrit: prāyaścittaṃ na tasyāsti yo dharmam atiśaṅkate dhyāyan sa kṛpaṇaḥ pāpo na lokān pratipadyate
english: There is no expiation for him who excessively doubts dharma; brooding, that wretch and sinner does not attain the higher worlds.

sanskrit: pramāṇāny ativṛtto hi vedaśāstrārthanindakaḥ kāmalobhānugo mūḍho narakaṃ pratipadyate
english: He who transgresses all authority, reviles the import of the Vedic scriptures, and follows desire and greed — that fool goes to hell.

sanskrit: yas tu nityaṃ kṛtamatir dharmam evābhipadyate aśaṅkamānaḥ kalyāṇi so 'mutrānantyam aśnute
english: But he who is always resolute in mind, who resorts to dharma alone without doubting, O auspicious one — he attains eternity in the world beyond.

sanskrit: ārṣaṃ pramāṇam utkramya dharmān aparipālayan sarvaśāstrātigo mūḍhaḥ śaṃ janmasu na vindati
english: He who transgresses the authority of the seers, does not protect the duties of dharma, and oversteps all scriptures — that fool finds no welfare across his births.

sanskrit: śiṣṭair ācaritaṃ dharmaṃ kṛṣṇe mā smātiśaṅkithāḥ purāṇam ṛṣibhiḥ proktaṃ sarvajñaiḥ sarvadarśibhiḥ
english: O Kṛṣṇā, do not excessively doubt the dharma practiced by the disciplined, the ancient teaching proclaimed by the all-knowing, all-seeing seers.

sanskrit: dharma eva plavo nānyaḥ svargaṃ draupadi gacchatām saiva nauḥ sāgarasyeva vaṇijaḥ pāram ṛcchataḥ
english: Dharma alone is the raft — there is no other — for those going to heaven, O Draupadī; it is the vessel, like a merchant's ship reaching the far shore of the ocean.

sanskrit: aphālo yadi dharmaḥ syāc carito dharmacāribhiḥ apratiṣṭhe tamasy etaj jagan majjed anindite
english: If dharma, when practiced by those who walk in dharma, were to bear no fruit, this blameless world would sink into groundless darkness.

sanskrit: nirvāṇaṃ nādhigaccheyur jīveyuḥ paśujīvikām vighātenaiva yujyeyur na cārthaṃ kiṃ cid āpnuyuḥ
english: Men would not attain liberation, they would live the life of beasts, they would be joined only with destruction, and they would attain nothing of value.

sanskrit: tapaś ca brahmacaryaṃ ca yajñaḥ svādhyāya eva ca dānam ārjavam etāni yadi syur aphalāni vai
english: Austerity, celibacy, sacrifice, study, generosity, and uprightness — if all these were indeed fruitless —

sanskrit: nācariṣyan pare dharmaṃ pare paratare ca ye vipralambho 'yam atyantaṃ yadi syur aphalāḥ kriyāḥ
english: — then neither those here nor those far beyond would practice dharma; this would be utter deceit if all these acts were fruitless.

sanskrit: ṛṣayaś caiva devāś ca gandharvāsurarākṣasāḥ īśvarāḥ kasya hetos te careyur dharmam ādṛtāḥ
english: The seers and the gods, the gandharvas, asuras, and rākṣasas — lords all — for what reason would they practice dharma with devotion?

sanskrit: phaladaṃ tv iha vijñāya dhātāraṃ śreyasi dhruve dharmaṃ te hy ācaran kṛṣṇe tad dhi dharmasanātanam
english: Knowing the Creator here to be the giver of fruit in the certain highest good, they practice dharma, O Kṛṣṇā — for that is the eternal dharma.

sanskrit: sa cāyaṃ saphalo dharmo na dharmo 'phala ucyate dṛśyante 'pi hi vidyānāṃ phalāni tapasāṃ tathā
english: And this dharma is indeed fruitful; dharma is not said to be fruitless — for the fruits of learning and likewise of austerities are visibly seen.

sanskrit: tvayy etad vai vijānīhi janma kṛṣṇe yathā śrutam vettha cāpi yathā jāto dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ pratāpavān
english: Know this to be so in your own case, O Kṛṣṇā, as it has been heard; you also know how the valiant Dhṛṣṭadyumna was born.

sanskrit: etāvad eva paryāptam upamānaṃ śucismite karmaṇāṃ phalam astīti dhīro 'lpenāpi tuṣyati
english: This much is sufficient illustration, O bright-smiling one — that there is fruit to actions; the wise man is satisfied even by a small example.

sanskrit: bahunāpi hy avidvāṃso naiva tuṣyanty abuddhayaḥ teṣāṃ na dharmajaṃ kiṃ cit pretya śarmāsti karma vā
english: For the ignorant who lack understanding are never satisfied even by much; for them there is no solace born of dharma or of action after death.

sanskrit: karmaṇām uta puṇyānāṃ pāpānāṃ ca phalodayaḥ prabhavaś cāpyayaś caiva devaguhyāni bhāmini
english: The arising of the fruit of actions — both meritorious and sinful — their origin and their dissolution: these are the secret mysteries of the gods, O passionate one.

sanskrit: naitāni veda yaḥ kaś cin muhyanty atra prajā imāḥ rakṣyāṇy etāni devānāṃ gūḍhamāyā hi devatāḥ
english: No one whatsoever knows these things — creatures are bewildered in this matter; these are to be kept hidden by the gods, for the deities have concealed their mysteries.

sanskrit: kṛśāṅgāḥ suvratāś caiva tapasā dagdhakilbiṣāḥ prasannair mānasair yuktāḥ paśyanty etāni vai dvijāḥ
english: Slender-limbed, of good vows, their sins burned away by austerity, endowed with serene minds — such brāhmaṇas indeed behold these things.

sanskrit: na phalādarśanād dharmaḥ śaṅkitavyo na devatāḥ yaṣṭavyaṃ cāpramattena dātavyaṃ cānasūyatā
english: Dharma should not be doubted because its fruit is not visible, nor should the gods be doubted; one should sacrifice with diligence and give without envy.

sanskrit: karmaṇāṃ phalam astīti tathaitad dharma śāśvatam brahmā provāca putrāṇāṃ yad ṛṣir veda kaśyapaḥ
english: "There is fruit to actions" — thus runs this eternal dharma; Brahmā declared it to his sons, and the seer Kaśyapa knows it.

sanskrit: tasmāt te saṃśayaḥ kṛṣṇe nīhāra iva naśyatu vyavasya sarvam astīti nāstikyaṃ bhāvam utsṛja
english: Therefore, O Kṛṣṇā, let your doubt vanish like mist; resolve that all this exists, and abandon the disposition of atheism.

sanskrit: īśvaraṃ cāpi bhūtānāṃ dhātāraṃ mā vicikṣipaḥ śikṣasvainaṃ namasvainaṃ mā te bhūd buddhir īdṛśī
english: Do not revile the Lord, the Creator of all beings; learn from Him, bow to Him — let such a disposition as this not be in you.

sanskrit: yasya prasādāt tadbhakto martyo gacchaty amartyatām uttamaṃ daivataṃ kṛṣṇe mātivocaḥ kathaṃ cana
english: By whose grace His devotee, though mortal, attains immortality — O Kṛṣṇā, do not speak ill in any way of that supreme divinity.

sanskrit: draupady uvāca nāvamanye na garhe ca dharmaṃ pārtha kathaṃ cana īśvaraṃ kuta evāham avamaṃsye prajāpatim
english: Draupadī said: I do not disrespect dharma, nor do I blame it in any way, O Pārtha; how should I disrespect the Lord, the Progenitor of creatures?

sanskrit: ārtāhaṃ pralapāmīdam iti māṃ viddhi bhārata bhūyaś ca vilapiṣyāmi sumanās tan nibodha me
english: Know me to be speaking thus in grief, O descendant of Bharata; and I shall lament yet further — hear that from me with a peaceful mind.

sanskrit: karma khalv iha kartavyaṃ jātenāmitrakarśana akarmāṇo hi jīvanti sthāvarā netare janāḥ
english: Action must indeed be performed in this world by one who is born, O crusher of foes; for it is only the immobile that live without action — not other beings.

sanskrit: ā mātṛstanapānāc ca yāvac chayyopasarpaṇam jaṅgamāḥ karmaṇā vṛttim āpnuvanti yudhiṣṭhira
english: From the drinking of the mother's breast right up to the approach of death's bed, mobile creatures gain their livelihood through action, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: jaṅgameṣu viśeṣeṇa manuṣyā bharatarṣabha icchanti karmaṇā vṛttim avāptuṃ pretya ceha ca
english: Among mobile creatures, men in particular, O bull of the Bhāratas, desire to obtain livelihood through action — both here and after death.

sanskrit: utthānam abhijānanti sarvabhūtāni bhārata pratyakṣaṃ phalam aśnanti karmaṇāṃ lokasākṣikam
english: All beings know exertion, O descendant of Bharata; they enjoy the visible fruit of actions, witnessed by the world.

sanskrit: paśyāmi svaṃ samutthānam upajīvanti jantavaḥ api dhātā vidhātā ca yathāyam udake bakaḥ
english: I see creatures living by their own exertion — even the Creator and the Ordainer do so, like this heron standing in the water.

sanskrit: svakarma kuru mā glāsīḥ karmaṇā bhava daṃśitaḥ kṛtyaṃ hi yo 'bhijānāti sahasre nāsti so 'sti vā
english: Perform your own duty; do not be despondent; be armored by action. For among a thousand men, he who knows what is to be done — whether he be or not — truly is.

sanskrit: tasya cāpi bhavet kāryaṃ vivṛddhau rakṣaṇe tathā bhakṣyamāṇo hy anāvāpaḥ kṣīyate himavān api
english: And even for him there would be something to be done — in increase and in protection; for even the Himālaya decays when eaten away without replenishment.

sanskrit: utsīderan prajāḥ sarvā na kuryuḥ karma ced yadi api cāpy aphalaṃ karma paśyāmaḥ kurvato janān nānyathā hy abhijānanti vṛttiṃ loke kathaṃ cana
english: All creatures would perish if they were not to perform action; and even if we see men performing action whose fruit is nil, they know no other way whatsoever to sustain life in this world.
